contentBlocks.title: Application Complete — Your Next Steps
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA application shows 'Application Complete' — all your details are verified and you're in the monthly evaluation cycle. Find out what happens next, when to expect your status update, and how to prepare for payment.

contentBlocks.text: The 'Application Complete' status is a positive sign. It means SASSA has received all your information, verified your details, and your profile is fully set up in the system. You are now in the monthly evaluation cycle where your eligibility is assessed each month.
This status affects applicants who have submitted all required documentation and SASSA is preparing a final decision.

contentBlocks.title: What Happens Next
contentBlocks.text: SASSA will make a final decision based on your submitted documents. Check your status regularly for the outcome.

contentBlocks.explanation: All verification steps — identity, bank, documents — have been completed successfully. Your application is no longer in 'Pending' status and is now part of the monthly automated approval system.
whyItHappens: Your initial application and documents have been fully processed
Your bank account verification was successful
Your identity was confirmed against Home Affairs records
Your profile is complete and ready for monthly evaluations
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: This status persists between monthly evaluation cycles. At the start of each month, it typically changes to 'Approved' or 'Declined' depending on that month's assessment.
whatYouShouldDo: Monitor the portal at the start of each month to see your status update
If it changes to 'Approved': check for your pay date
If it changes to 'Declined': review the reason and file an appeal if needed
Ensure your bank account remains active and your contact details stay current
whatToCheck: Check the portal to ensure both banking details and personal details show verified checkmarks.
Monitor your status weekly as it moves from Complete to Approved during the monthly run.

contentBlocks.text: Illustrative example: complete on the 27th, approved on the 2nd

On 27 October, Palesa's status moved from Pending to Application Complete. Nothing was left for her to submit: identity had matched, the bank account had verified, and the documents were accepted. The status sat still for six days, then changed to Approved in the first days of November when the monthly assessment ran.

The mistake to avoid in this window is treating 'complete' as 'paid'. It is a readiness state. It means there is nothing outstanding on your side and the next monthly decision can be made — not that the decision has been made, and not that money is scheduled.

contentBlocks.text: What SASSA confirms before a file is complete

A file becomes complete when the identity check against the Home Affairs record, the bank account verification and the submitted documents have all been accepted. General documentation requirements are published at sassa.gov.za, and the identity and banking requirements are described on the SRD portal. Because each month is assessed separately, a complete file still has to clear the income check for the month in question.

faqs.question: Does 'Application Complete' mean I will definitely get paid?
faqs.answer: Almost always, yes, provided your means test does not fail during the final monthly bank sweep. Most applicants with 'Application Complete' status proceed to 'Approved'.

faqs.question: How long does 'Application Complete' last?
faqs.answer: It stays active until the monthly evaluation cycle begins. At the start of the next month, it will change to either 'Approved' or 'Declined'.

faqs.question: Can 'Application Complete' change back to 'Pending'?
faqs.answer: It should not. If your status reverts to 'Pending', it may indicate a document or verification issue that needs attention.
